deck_title: Kingslake macro bellows effective aperture vs naive infinity f-number deficit rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Rudolf Kingslake (1951, Lenses in Photography) macro bellows effective f-number law (N_eff = v / D = N * (1 + m), where image distance v = f*(1 + m) increases with transverse magnification m, compensating sensor exposure by the bellows factor B = (1 + m)^2 = 1 + u to lock irradiance at E/E_target = 1.0000x across all 17 macro stations u in [0.0000, 1.0000] with 0/17 underexposed stations) versus naive infinity-focus nominal f-number (N = f / D, which ignores the inverse-square solid-angle drop of the extended exit pupil and incurs an exposure deficit of (1 + m)^2 = 1 + u up to 1.2500x at u=0.25, 1.5000x at u=0.50, and 2.0000x at u=1.00 across 16/17 stations) and 64-ring exit-pupil radiometric integration.
